content: Advanced Practice Nurses (APNs) are Registered Nurses who have undergone advanced education and training, both in theoretical knowledge and clinical practice. They possess specialized skills and operate within an expanded scope of practice. The term Advanced Practice Nurse encompasses four distinct graduate-level nursing roles: Nurse Practitioners, Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists, Clinical Nurse Specialists, and Certified Nurse Midwives. In the United States, most APNs are educated at the graduate level, typically earning a Master of Science in Nursing (MSN). However, many APNs pursue doctoral-level education, obtaining a Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP or DrNP). While a doctorate is not currently a mandatory requirement to become an APN, the American Association of Colleges of Nursing (AACN) has recommended that by 2015, the DNP should become the minimum academic requirement for advanced nursing practice. This clinical doctorate is a professional degree focused on practice-based expertise. The DNP requirement applies only to new entrants into the APN field; those already licensed and practicing with a master’s degree are not required to pursue additional education under a grandfather clause. Some APNs have been grandfathered into the profession, meaning they entered the field before graduate degrees were required. For instance, the first Nurse Practitioner program, established in 1965 at the University of Colorado by Loretta C. Ford, EdD, RN, PNP, and Henry K. Silver, MD, was a certificate program designed to train Registered Nurses for advanced roles as Pediatric Nurse Practitioners in response to a shortage of primary care physicians. APNs or individuals in similar advanced nursing roles can pursue terminal degrees, which represent the highest level of academic achievement in a field. Examples of terminal degrees include the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Doctor of Nursing Science (DNSc), Doctor of Education (EdD), and Doctor of Science (DSc). Common post-nominal initials include: CRNP: Certified Registered Nurse Practitioner ARNP: Advanced Registered Nurse Practitioner CRNA: Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist CNM: Certified Nurse Midwife CNS: Clinical Nurse Specialist APRN: Advanced Practice Registered Nurse FNP: Family Nurse Practitioner PNP: Pediatric Nurse Practitioner WHNP: Women’s Health Nurse Practitioner NNP: Neonatal Nurse Practitioner PMHNP: Psychiatric & Mental Health Nurse Practitioner PsyNP: Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner GNP: Gerontological Nurse Practitioner ACNP: Acute Care Nurse Practitioner ANP: Adult Nurse Practitioner ONP: Oncology Nurse Practitioner C or BC: Certified or Board Certified (e.g., APRN-BC, FNP-BC, FNP-C, GNP-C, ANP-BC) NP-C: Nurse Practitioner Certified CS: Clinical Specialist These designations reflect the specific expertise, certifications, and roles of Advanced Practice Nurses within the healthcare system.
